title: Worktree and task coordination
summary: Split work into dependency-ordered tasks with non-overlapping file ownership, one worktree per task, explicit handoffs and conflict detection before integration.

provenance.notes: ECC's worktree orchestrator is a script; here only the planning discipline is adopted, and execution stays with the existing scheduler.

inputs.name: objective
inputs.description: The objective to split into tasks.

outputs.name: task-graph
outputs.description: Tasks with acceptance criteria, allowed files, dependencies and owners.

workflow.step: Break the objective into tasks small enough to verify independently; write acceptance criteria and allowed files for each.
Record dependencies as a DAG and reject cycles.
Detect overlapping allowed files between tasks that could run in parallel; serialize or merge overlapping tasks.
workflow.check: No two concurrent tasks own the same file.

workflow.step: Give every task its own worktree and a named owner; record handoffs and what each receiver must re-verify.
workflow.check: Ownership is unambiguous at every moment.

workflow.step: Before integration, rebase or merge in dependency order and rerun the verifiers on the integrated result.

constraints: Do not build a competing scheduler; plans feed the existing one.
Never touch another session's worktree or force-push.
A plan does not grant any task additional files.

examples.title: Shared helper
examples.situation: Two parallel tasks both need to edit the same helper file.
examples.guidance: Serialize them, or extract the helper change as a first task both depend on.

verification: The graph is acyclic and file ownership is disjoint for concurrent tasks.
Integration reruns verifiers on the merged result.

task.text: Decompose into parallel tasks as a dag with file ownership and avoid merge conflict in each worktree.
Coordinate the handoff between worktrees and run the integration.
